name: SISO People Graph
summary: One canonical graph of people who produced something, joining a person's identities across GitHub, books, crates.io and video into a single person identity with typed edges to their works.

evidence.summary: The repository holds the schema and loaders in git while the graph itself ships as a release asset. Release graph-v2 was downloaded to a clean directory, decompressed and queried: person=339217, person_person=1272495, organisation=1131. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-07 by PG-BASELINE against the real shipped asset (people_graph_v2.sqlite.gz, 278,859,777 bytes, gz SHA-256 85a0f1e4f44ae4b5843be919bee236146b8fe73bb3bf67928f6a1507be557a3c; decompressed 1,113,350,144 bytes, db SHA-256 9938237a33277fe3a29a278d68c361a1f300d9060740cc2e917920157d9b919b) at repo commit de048bb3b34bf931b56fd741cb46c1334acdfb98, the exact commit GQ-010 source_scopes pins. The person count is correct. A 2026-08-07 amendment had downgraded this to a repository claim on the grounds that 339217 appears in no tracked file; that search was sound but not decisive, because the figure is stated in the graph-v2 RELEASE TITLE, which is not a tracked file. Receipt: GQ-010-BASELINE.html section 3.1. Both digests are pinned deliberately: the asset is mutable by design, so any re-measurement must confirm it compares the same bytes.

license.reason: No license has been selected for this repository. The graph aggregates metadata from sources with differing terms, including Project Gutenberg catalog metadata, GitHub repository metadata, and the crates.io database dump whose own README states no license at all. Rights must be resolved per source scope before any redistribution claim is made.

evidence.summary: No LICENSE file is present in the repository root listing, which contains only .gitignore, README.md, loaders and schema. Public visibility is therefore not a reuse grant, consistent with the Library's own pending-license posture.

relationships.context: The graph is built by loaders that live in the Foundry pipelines tree. Foundry owns source discovery and evaluation; the people graph owns canonical person identity and the edges to what each person produced. Physical co-location of the checkouts does not imply containment.

evidence.summary: Twenty-two loaders under pipelines/ write into the graph, sharing one contract: a read-only source argument, a --graph target, --limit and --apply. Three create people; the remainder enrich existing people or derive structure from what is already loaded.

The published graph-v2 asset was retrieved to a clean directory and queried: 339,217 people, 901,524 person-to-work edges, 1,272,495 person_person rows, 1,131 organisations and 442,499 external identities. VERIFIED 2026-08-07 by PG-BASELINE directly against the shipped 1.1 GB database (db SHA-256 9938237a33277fe3a29a278d68c361a1f300d9060740cc2e917920157d9b919b), superseding an earlier same-day amendment that had treated these as unverified repository claims. CORRECTION IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, same section: the 1,272,495 figure is real but MISLABELLED here and in the release title. Every one of those rows is relation='depends_on', source='crates_io_dependencies', at a flat confidence of 0.95 -- they are crates.io PACKAGE DEPENDENCIES projected onto owners, not human person-to-person relations. Package A depending on package B implies no relationship between their owners, and the flat confidence carries no discriminating information. This is the owner-to-creator category collapse the programme's own diagnosis names. Do not cite this layer as a social or who-knows-whom graph. Receipt: GQ-010-BASELINE.html section 3.3. Note also that four shipped tables (person_person, organisation, organisation_content, person_organisation) appear in no tracked schema, and 86.7% of person rows are kind='unknown'.

The relational layer is derived from 32,243,556 declared package dependency rows, of which 27,847,334 runtime edges were kept and 4,396,222 development and build edges deliberately excluded as a different claim. An edge therefore means one person's software does not build without another's, which is machine-checked rather than inferred. It answers who is load-bearing rather than who is popular: the most depended-upon person is relied on by 45,037 distinct others. Two earlier attempts at this layer were measured and rejected, one yielding 720,107,620 meaningless co-membership pairs and one yielding five usable edges.

Membership is evidence-led rather than popularity-led. 58,509 people were admitted because a third party measured use of their published work, not because their repositories cleared a 100-star threshold; the preceding population matched that threshold to within nine people. Among those admitted are maintainers of infrastructure with billions of recorded installs whose repositories fall below the threshold, which is the case against it. People whose output is not yet linked are recorded as tracked rather than omitted.

The schema encodes the graph's design laws: satellites are referenced rather than duplicated, so content_ref holds a repository name or catalog identifier and the bytes stay in the domain that owns them; every cross-source match is an explicit, evidenced, reversible identity_claim rather than a silent merge; role sits on the edge rather than the person; and person.state distinguishes a tracked person with no linked output from a broken row.

Fifteen enrichment rounds are recorded with the command and raw output behind every number, including three negative results that stopped expensive work: a GitHub-to-book identity stitch capped at 419 candidate people and yielding zero plausible matches, naive person-to-person co-membership measured at 720,107,620 pairs and rejected, and a repository source-diversity signal shown to be a restatement of stars once controlled for.
